title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory
by: Preston Rasmussen, Pavlo Paliychuk, Travis Beauvais, Jack Ryan, Daniel Chalef (Zep AI), January 2025. Read in full from the arXiv PDF (v1), including the appendix prompts.
summary: Zep is a memory service built on Graphiti, a knowledge graph with three layers: episodes (the raw messages, kept unchanged), entities and facts extracted from them, and communities (clusters of entities with summaries). Every fact carries two timelines: when it held in the world and when the system recorded or retired it. When a new fact contradicts an old one, the old one is not deleted; its end date is set to the new fact's start date. On LongMemEval it beats passing the whole conversation, with about 90% lower latency.
ideas: Episodes are the non-lossy store: every derived fact keeps a two-way index to the episodes it came from, so it can be cited or quoted back.
Bi-temporal model: t_valid and t_invalid say when a fact was true in the world; t'_created and t'_expired say when Zep learned it and when it stopped believing it.

Each message has a reference time, used to turn 'two weeks ago' or 'next Thursday' into absolute dates; the prompt sets valid_at to the reference time for present-tense facts and leaves dates null when none are stated.

Invalidation: a model compares a new fact with related existing facts; for a contradiction that overlaps in time, the old fact's t_invalid is set to the new fact's t_valid. The paper says it 'consistently prioritizes new information' by ingestion order.

Deduplication is narrowed by structure: a new fact is only compared with facts between the same two entities, which cuts errors and cost. Writes to the graph use fixed, predefined Cypher queries, not model-written queries.
Retrieval returns each fact with its valid date range in the context string, so the answering model sees when each fact held.

Measured: DMR 94.8% vs MemGPT's reported 93.4% (gpt-4-turbo), but full conversation scores 94.4% there and 98.0% vs Zep 98.2% with gpt-4o-mini, so DMR barely separates anything. LongMemEval (about 115k tokens): 71.2% vs 60.2% full context with gpt-4o, 63.8% vs 55.4% with gpt-4o-mini, context 1.6k vs 115k tokens.

Caveats the authors state: DMR conversations fit in context and its questions are vague; Zep lost 9 to 18% on single-session-assistant questions; they could not run MemGPT on LongMemEval. All numbers are their own runs.

took.idea: Keep 'when it held' apart from 'when we wrote it'; a doc has a validity range and the write has a timestamp
A contradiction closes the old doc's range at the new doc's start instead of deleting it
Every derived doc points back to the raw record (episode) it came from
Compare a new doc only with docs about the same subject, and write through fixed code paths, never model-written queries
Return the validity range with every doc a read returns
